title: Prometheus fanout + log-forwarding playbook (private deployments)
content:
Goal: define a low-risk, repeatable playbook for shipping metrics and logs from private/VPC deployments to our observability backbone while preserving tenant isolation, predictable cost, and upgradeability. Focus is on Prometheus fanout/sharding, Grafana access patterns, OTEL collector log pipelines (buffering & backpressure), and Terraform module considerations for customers in air-gapped or VPC-restricted environments.

Context / Motivation:
- Customers on Private mode currently run a single Prometheus scrape or light federation. That doesn’t scale for high-cardinality workloads and makes upgrades risky (single node changes).
- We need a pattern for: (a) horizontal scaling of ingest (sharding/fanout), (b) durable buffering of logs/traces in networks with egress controls, (c) secure long-term archive (S3-compatible with KMS), and (d) Terraform modules customers can consume with minimal boilerplate.

Non-goals:
- Not prescribing specific vendor (Thanos/VM/ Cortex) as final choice here — instead outline modular options and tradeoffs.
- Not covering end-user dashboard design (Grafana content will be separate).

Architecture sketch (textual):
1) Metrics: local-prometheus (customer) -> vmagent (push/remote_write distributor) -> short-term hot layer (local Prometheus or vmstorage) + remote_write fanout to upstream ingestion cluster (private control plane) -> object store for long-term (Thanos/VM-S3)
2) Logs: fluent-bit (edge) -> local OTEL-collector (log receiver & processor) -> persistent buffer (disk / local.kafka) -> push to secure egress proxy -> central log-acceptor (OTLP/HTTP) -> long-term archive (S3)
3) Traces: OTEL-collector sidecar -> jaeger/tempo-compatible acceptor in central control plane (OTLP over GRPC for backpressure)

Key design choices and rationale:
- Fanout vs federation: fanout (vmagent or Prometheus remote_write) provides lower read cost on the central side and better control over per-tenant throttling. Federation keeps raw scrape semantics but is heavier on central storage. For private deployments we recommend vmagent-based remote_write fanout by default.
- Durable buffering for logs: prefer OTEL collector with file-based or disk queue before egress to handle transient connectivity loss. Avoid unbounded memory queues.
- Auth & encryption: all egress must go via customer-managed NAT/EGress proxy; use mTLS between OTEL/remote_write clients and Redwoods’ ingestion endpoints. KMS-wrapped object storage keys for S3 archive.

Terraform module notes (customer-facing module: rwi/private-observability):
- Inputs to expose: enable_metrics (bool), enable_logs (bool), prometheus_scrape_configs (list of maps as yaml), remote_write_endpoint (string), remote_write_token_secret_arn (string), otel_collector_image (string), log_bucket_name (string), kms_key_arn (string), buffer_disk_size_gb (number), egress_proxy_endpoint (string)
- Outputs to return: prometheus_service_name, otel_collector_service_account, log_bucket_arn, iam_role_for_remote_write
- Important IAM boundaries: separate role for metrics vs logs so customer can audit and rotate keys independently. Provide example policies in module docs.
- Module patterns: use a "sidecar" module (container + systemd/k8s DaemonSet) for OTEL collector and vmagent so customers can integrate with k8s or systemd-based installs.
- Migration-friendly flags: add toggle variables for using vmagent vs direct Prometheus remote_write; allow 'dry-run' mode where remote_write goes to a staging endpoint for validation.

Upgrade strategy (high-level plan):
- Phase 0: Canary deploy fanout path to 5% of hosts — route only low-cardinality metrics. Validate CPU/memory and remote_write retries.
- Phase 1: Enable full remote_write for a non-critical tenant group; monitor duplicates, ingestion latency, and downstream cost.
- Phase 2: Cutover logs: run OTEL-collector in dual-write mode (local + remote) for 24–72h, then flip primary.
- Phase 3: Decommission local retention beyond minimal hot window (e.g., 6hrs) once remote ingestion + hot store confirmed. Keep rollback path for 7 days where dual-write can be re-enabled.

Operational playbook (runbook bullets):
- Pre-upgrade checks: ensure S3 lifecycle policy exists, KMS key policy includes our ingestion role, egress proxy reachable (curl test), disk buffer has >= 2x expected backfill capacity.
- Live upgrade checklist: drain vmagent queue, scale new vmagent horizontally with consistent scrape configs, verify remote_write 200 responses for every replica via /metrics endpoint exposure (vmagent exposes remote_write metrics).
- Post-upgrade verification: compare series counts (prometheus tsdb series) pre/post across a sample of metrics; validate alerting rules fire/noise within expected thresholds.

Failure modes we need to plan for:
- Remote_write 429s: need per-tenant retry backoff. Add jitter and exponential backoff in vmagent; surface 429 ratio to Ops dashboard.
- Disk buffer exhaustion: collector should switch to tail-drop with alert; alert should include disk usage and earliest-possible data-loss window.
- Blackhole egress (network misconfig): automated fail-open not acceptable; we should fallback to local retention and route alerts to SRE to avoid silent loss.

Monitoring & dashboards (suggested):
- Collector health: up status, queue length (seconds), disk usage, last successful push timestamp.
- vmagent metrics: remote_write success/failure counts, per-destination latencies, dropped samples.
- Ingestion side: per-tenant token usage, 429 rate, series-per-minute deltas.

Security / compliance notes:
- All ingress tokens are stored as customer-managed secrets; provide example to use KMS or Vault.
- Audit logs: Terraform should create CloudTrail/S3 bucket access logging (or equivalent) with 90d retention by default.

Open questions / TODO:
- Decide canonical distributor: vmagent vs Cortex/Distributor. Need benchmarking for high-cardinality workloads (RDOPS-2145).
- Do we provide an opinionated Loki/Tempo stack or remain agnostic? (impact on Terraform surfaces).
- Edge-case: Air-gapped installs with no egress — propose an appliance-mode bundle with removable storage shipping (offline ingestion), but that requires a separate playbook and legal review.

Quick command snippets (examples for k8s-based private deployments):
- Deploy vmagent DaemonSet skeleton: kubectl apply -f vmagent-daemonset.yaml (vmagent config mounts prometheus scrape configs)
- Check remote_write targets (inside vmagent metrics): kubectl exec -c vmagent pod -- curl -s localhost:8429/metrics | grep remote_write
- Disk-buffer verify for OTEL collector: kubectl exec collector-pod -- du -sh /var/lib/otel-buffer

Notes to authors: keep this doc light and developer-oriented. We should roll this into a single Terraform module repo with example k8s overlays and a small test harness to simulate 5% canary traffic. Attach benchmark results to GH PR.

Author: Maya Chen (eng-private-deployments). Draft and will sync with Diego, Priya, and SRE leads next week.

Last edits: added dual-write upgrade pattern and explicit terraform input list on 2026-02-28.
